safe_temperature.temperature: 145°F (62.8°C) with a 3-minute rest time for all whole fresh cuts; 160°F (71.1°C) for ground pork

source.name: Know Your Pork Cuts - National Pork Board & USDA Guidelines

safe_temperature.disagreements: The USDA and National Pork Board updated the safe cooking temperature for whole pork cuts (chops, roasts, tenderloins) from 160°F down to 145°F followed by a mandatory 3-minute rest period. At 145°F, pork remains slightly pink in the center and retains natural juiciness; cooking lean pork to 160°F produces dry, tough, and chalky meat. However, for tough collagen-rich cuts (shoulder, butt, belly, ribs), notebook sources deliberately depart from 145°F and slow-cook meat to internal temperatures of 195°F–205°F to melt connective tissue into fall-apart shreddable pork or render crackling skin.

methods.cut: bone-in or boneless pork chops (1 to 1.5 inches thick, center-cut or loin chops)
methods.heat: Medium-high heat in heavy skillet (cast-iron preferred); finish covered on low or in 375°F oven
methods.time: 2 to 3 minutes per side sear, then 6 to 10 minutes covered on low heat (or in 375°F oven)
methods.doneness: Internal temperature reads 145°F in the thickest part; meat is slightly pink and juices run clear
methods.rest: 3 to 5 minutes on a warm plate
methods.tips: Pat chops dry before searing; hold chops upright with tongs for 30 seconds to render and brown the exterior fat cap; remove chops from pan, add butter and garlic to pan drippings, and deglaze with apple cider vinegar, wine, or broth for an instant pan sauce.

source.name: The Best Juicy Skillet Pork Chops Recipe - Inspired Taste & Recipe Teacher

methods.cut: whole pork tenderloin (trimmed of silverskin, approx. 1 to 1.25 lbs)
methods.heat: Medium heat skillet sear, then transferred to 400°F (205°C) oven
methods.time: 2 minutes per side sear in skillet (approx. 6 to 8 minutes total), then 10 to 15 minutes roast in oven
methods.doneness: Instant-read thermometer reads 145°F to 150°F in thickest section; tender and juicy with slight pink blush
methods.rest: 5 to 10 minutes tented with foil before slicing
methods.tips: Always trim the tough white silverskin with a sharp boning knife; sear meat on all sides before applying spice rubs or herb crusts so the spices do not scorch in the pan; slice against the grain into thick medallions.

source.name: Best Juicy Pork Tenderloin Recipe - Inspired Taste & The Kitchn

methods.cut: skin-on pork shoulder roast or skin-on pork belly
methods.heat: 320°F (160°C) slow roast for 2.5 hours, then blasted at 485°F (250°C) for 25 to 30 minutes
methods.doneness: Internal temperature reaches 195°F–205°F; flesh is fall-apart succulent and skin is transformed into blistered, shatter-crisp crackling
methods.rest: 15 to 20 minutes loosely tented with foil (thick crackling will not soften)
methods.tips: The four non-negotiable rules for crackling skin are surface area, dryness, salt, and heat; score skin with a sharp knife, scald with boiling water, dry thoroughly with paper towels, and rub coarse salt deep into cuts; blast at high heat at the very end to puff and bubble the rind.

source.name: Pork Roast with Crispy Crackling - RecipeTin Eats & Tasting Table

methods.cut: St. Louis style spareribs or baby back ribs (racks)
methods.heat: 300°F (150°C) covered, then 425°F (218°C) or broil for glazing
methods.time: 2.5 to 3 hours tightly wrapped in foil, then 10 to 15 minutes uncovered with barbecue sauce glaze
methods.doneness: Meat shrinks back 1/4 inch from bone tips and bends with slight crack in surface
methods.rest: 10 to 15 minutes before slicing between bones
methods.tips: Peel off the tough papery membrane from the bone side of the ribs before cooking for maximum tenderness and rub penetration; wrap tightly in heavy-duty foil to lock in steam and braise the meat in its own juices.

source.name: The Ultimate Guide to Pork Ribs - Smithfield

methods.cut: boneless or bone-in pork shoulder / Boston butt (cut into large chunks)
methods.heat: Low heat slow cooker (approx. 200°F) or 325°F covered Dutch oven
methods.time: 6 to 8 hours on low in slow cooker (or 2.5 to 3 hours in 325°F Dutch oven)
methods.doneness: Internal temperature reaches 200°F–205°F; meat shreds effortlessly with two forks
methods.rest: 10 minutes resting in braising liquid before shredding
methods.tips: Rub pork with brown sugar, smoked paprika, cumin, and garlic; add apple cider vinegar and sliced onions; after shredding, toss pulled pork back into pan juices to keep it juicy.

source.name: Slow Cooker Pulled Pork (Easy Recipe) - Fifteen Spatulas

Dark brown sugar and dry mustard powder
Coarse sea salt and cracked black pepper

Dijon mustard and pure maple syrup
Rich pan gravy from roast drippings

avoid.warning: Overcooking lean pork cuts (chops, tenderloin) past 145°F: lean pork has little fat; cooking to 160°F expels all moisture, leaving it dry, chalky, and tough.
Leaving the tough silverskin on pork tenderloin: silverskin is elastin connective tissue that does not break down during quick cooking and contracts into a tough, chewy strip.
Leaving the membrane on the underside of ribs: the papery membrane prevents seasonings and smoke from penetrating and turns leathery when baked.
Searing meat wet: moisture prevents browning; pat meat thoroughly dry before searing.
